# StateWeave

> StateWeave is a low-level TypeScript SDK for persistent agents built on an immutable causal graph. The graph is canonical truth; each model prompt is a bounded projection. The public SDK has one agent class: Agent.

## Start

- [Introduction](https://stateweave.dev/introduction): What StateWeave is, the one principle, and ownership boundaries.
- [Quickstart](https://stateweave.dev/quickstart): Build from source, run a deterministic agent, persist state, and connect a provider.

## Understand

- [Why StateWeave](https://stateweave.dev/concepts/why-stateweave): Why durable state and model context are different objects.
- [Nodes](https://stateweave.dev/concepts/nodes): The ten node kinds, frontier, resource versions, and semantic memory.
- [One turn](https://stateweave.dev/concepts/the-turn): Append, projection, action, verification evidence, and transactional commit.
- [Projection](https://stateweave.dev/concepts/projection): Deterministic big-brain, peripheral, focus, and timeline layers for a bounded prompt.

## Build

- [Tools](https://stateweave.dev/guides/tools): Zod tools and the safe default workspace tools.
- [Models](https://stateweave.dev/guides/models): The provider-neutral Model interface, included adapters, and provider token events.
- [Persist and stream](https://stateweave.dev/guides/persist-and-stream): State ownership, concurrency, token/engine events, and failure.
- [Complete agent](https://stateweave.dev/examples/complete-agent): A server-owned integration and coding-agent variant.

## Reference

- [Agent API](https://stateweave.dev/reference/agent): Constructor, methods, defaults, results, and AgentRunError.
- [Types and exports](https://stateweave.dev/reference/types): Public state, model, tool, stream, graph, and low-level exports.

## Source

- [TypeScript SDK](https://github.com/stateweave/sdk-typescript)
- [Documentation source](https://github.com/stateweave/docs)

The initial npm package publication is pending authenticated npm ownership. Do not present `pnpm add stateweave` as available until the package exists.
